subject: Outrage as Georgetown students reportedly plan Charlie Kirk ‘lookalike contest’ on assassination anniversary
posts:
Georgetown students spark fierce outrage by allegedly organizing a Charlie Kirk lookalike contest on his assassination anniversary.
Evidence: anonymous Fizz app posts, thousands of upvotes
#Aletheia #Georgetown #CultureWars

Promoters defended the stunt as edgy campus satire and free expression.
Stated Judgement: (0.0, 0.0) — Neutral Stasis

In reality, mocking a political assassination poisons campus discourse and weaponizes grief for online validation.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.75, -0.8) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Turning tragedy into dark satirical spectacle degrades shared humanity.
Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 6.2, z: 2)

- Georgetown Student Organizers: FAIL (-0.75, -0.8) — Weaponizes tragic death for anonymous clout.
- Turning Point USA Chapter: PASS (0.6, 0.5) — Defends basic human decency and mourning.
The controversial contest was promoted on Fizz, an anonymous campus app, garnering thousands of upvotes ahead of the one-year mark of Kirk's death.

The Poison:
Toxic campus tribalism erodes basic empathy, replacing constructive political debate with gleeful mockery of violence.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing digital provocation (HOW) with genuine moral critique (WHY).

Social Physics Analysis:
Students run a Smart Selfish Maneuver, using anonymous platforms to manufacture inflammatory spectacles for tribal clout while projecting blame for campus hostility onto opponents.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Cruel spectacle deepens cultural fractures.

The Unavoidable Truth: Anonymous campus platforms frequently amplify callous trolling that mocks real-world violence.

The Unavoidable Lie: Cruel anniversary mockery constitutes noble free expression.
